acceptanceCriteria: A docs/build-log-only change binds without a spec intent and the sealed map carries class `record`; `tools/cem-citation-baseline` reports `record` rows apart from `change`; the DCW spec names the class and the baseline registration (0527) states whether record maps are excluded from the authored arm.
body:
Observed friction. PR beamfall/corvint#855 added only a build-log entry and three evidence files. `dogfood change` refused the build-log entry as intent (ocm-prepare invalid-requirements-section: the intent must be a spec with exactly one `## Requirements` heading) and refused a uniform plan (DCW-V0-048), so the bind cited DCW-V0-052, -053, -055 and -056 one span per hunk by convention, not because the hunks implement those requirements. The same pattern applies to every docs-only record change (S1..S3 build-log entries, baseline records). These citations are exactly the shape the V1-1336/V1-1278 baselines measure as 'no better than a grep bot' (authored excess 1.94%, kill under 0527): the recipe manufactures weak citations.

Expected: a third citation class beside `change` and `chore` (DCW-V0-048/049), e.g. `record`, for a change whose paths are all under docs/build-log/ (and its evidence/ subtree) or .agent-evidence/: the map binds the hunks to the build-log entry (or to the decision it records) with relation `evidence`, no spec span required, and the baseline tool reports the class separately so record maps stop diluting the authored arm.
Actual: record changes must cite spec spans; builders choose spans mechanically.

Version: origin/main 88197e465 (2026-10-13). Source: SDD review by the orchestrating session for decisions 0523/0525 after PRs #850..#855.
title: dogfood: an evidence-record change (build-log entry + evidence files) has no requirement to cite; add a `record` citation class instead of forcing spec spans
